text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Elevated DNS errors observed for eu-* edge; 5xx-equivalent resolver errors at 23% (threshold 5%) — paging oncall.

maria gonzales: seeing the same — multiple customers reporting site assets 404 and some embedded widgets failing in EU. hitting old A records for api.redwood.example.com in some probes.

sam (oncall): on it. tagging network: @jon lee. Maria, can you paste the probe examples and when this started?

maria gonzales: started ~ 6954321200 (10m ago). samples: traceroute and dig from eu-fr probe ->
```
; dig +short api.redwood.example.com @1.1.1.1
203.0.113.5
; dig +short api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8
198.51.100.7
```
One region returns our new A (203.0.113.5) and another returns old (198.51.100.7) which is decommissioned. Cloudflare proxied and Route53 authoritative.

jon lee: hunch: Cloudflare geo-steering / cache + route53 latency causing split answers. Could be Cloudflare resolver or one of their edge PoPs holding stale records for EU. I’ll query CF and route53 from multiple EU probes.

sam (oncall): next steps: 1) confirm consumer impact (SLA/customer-facing) 2) attempt Cloudflare cache purge for the fqdn 3) if unsuccessful, temporarily shift geo-dns mapping to Route53 health-based failover for EU 4) open CF support ticket and escalate.

support-ops: confirming impact: we've got 12% of EU requests failing validation checks on RN side, ~8 customers with degraded UX (assets failing). classify as P1/P2? I’d call it P2 because partial region impact but broad customer effect.

maria gonzales: I've opened a support case with Cloudflare and attached probe logs: https://support.cloudflare.com/tickets/RC-12345 (internal ref). CF-bot acknowledged.

cloudflare-support-bot: We received RC-12345. Investigating edge caching and geo-routing for your zone redwood.example.com. We'll update within 15 minutes.

jon lee: running parallel checks. from eu-de and eu-fr, querying authoritative directly (Route53) returns correct A (203.0.113.5). Cloudflare edge returns mixed. Looks like some CF PoPs have stale DNS cache/inconsistent RRset.

sam (oncall): Maria — can you attempt an immediate Cloudflare cache purge for hostname? Use dashboard or API, but note purging at DNS level isn't standard; purge of CF workers/edge cache might help for proxied records. Try zone cache purge and also request CF to flush DNS cache for specific PoPs via ticket.

maria gonzales: running API purge now:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<ZONE_ID>/purge_cache" \
 -H "X-Auth-Email: ops@redwood.com" \
 -H "X-Auth-Key: <REDACTED>" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 --data '{"files":["https://api.redwood.example.com/*"]}'
```
Response: 200 accepted. Also added note to ticket requesting DNS cache flush from EU PoPs.

jon lee: purge acknowledged. probing again... some PoPs now return correct IP, but eu-west-2 (some nodes) still return 198.51.100.7.

sam (oncall): CF saying they’re flushing but propagation to all PoPs may lag. We need a fallback if this doesn't converge in 10–15m. Recommend toggling geo-dns to prefer Route53 for EU via our geo-policy: set Route53 weight to 100 for eu-geo record and reduce TTL to 60. Prepare change, will apply if CF doesn't resolve in 15m.

maria gonzales: preparing Route53 change now. change batch draft:
```
ChangeResourceRecordSetsRequest:
 - Delete: CNAME api.redwood.example.com -> cloudflare-proxy.redwood.example.com
 - Create: A api.redwood.example.com (eu) -> 203.0.113.5 (weight=100, set-identifier="eu-failover")
 - TTL: 60
```
Will wait 10m for CF confirmation before apply; will coordinate rollback plan.

ryan k: pinging product/comms — we should prep a short status-page blurb: "Partial DNS resolution issues affecting EU region sites; investigating; potential mitigation underway". Avoid announcing routing changes until confirmed.

support-ops: we’ve drafted an incident severity banner S2 and short impact note. ready to post if we flip to Route53.

cloudflare-support-bot: Update on RC-12345: We observed an internal cache replication lag between some EU PoPs and our DNS authoritative layer. Flushing targeted PoPs now; estimated full convergence 7–12 minutes.

sam (oncall): CF ETA OK. Hold on Route53 switch for now. Maria keep probing; Jon keep CF ticket hot. If we see no decrease in customer errors by 10 minutes from now we execute Route53 change and update status page.

maria gonzales: probes show error rate dropping — 23% -> 6% over last 4m. CF ticket shows targeted PoP flush completed for eu-west nodes.

jon lee: confirming across probes: eu-* convergence looks nearly complete. spot checks: all returning 203.0.113.5 now.

sam (oncall): Good. Canceling Route53 switch. actions: 1) monitor for 30m 2) keep CF ticket open until we see full 60m stable 3) add regression alert to catch recurrence 4) record RCA notes. Maria, please summarize cause and steps for postmortem.

maria gonzales: summary draft for PM: root cause: Cloudflare DNS cache replication lag led to inconsistent RRset propagation across EU PoPs causing partial resolution to decommissioned IP. Mitigation: CF PoP flush + API purge; CF performed targeted PoP cache flush; monitored probes until convergence. Work items: add monitoring for DNS RRset divergence, automate CF ticket escalation, review geo-dns fallback runbook and test Route53 failover in staging.

sam (oncall): handing off to @jon lee for monitoring for the next 2 hours, then to night oncall. Jon, accept handoff?

jon lee: taking handoff — will watch for 2h and will escalate if error rate >3% for >10m. I’ll also keep the CF ticket open.

maria gonzales: I'll add the incident to the postmortem tracker and tag "dns/geo". thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam (oncall): closing pager for now. If anyone observes a regression, @jon lee is primary for next 2h and then night oncall. Filing incident stub (INC-2026-042) and will expand postmortem.
